title: Residue-Specific Exchange of Proline by Proline Analogs in Fluorescent Proteins: How "Molecular Surgery" of the Backbone Affects Folding and Stability
protocol: Mix 1 ng of each sample plasmid pQE-80L H6-EGFP with 50 µL of chemically competent or electrocompetent cells of Pro-auxotrophic E. coli K12-derived strain JM83 for transformation by the heat shock method or electroporation.

Mix 1 ng of each sample plasmid pQE-80L H6-NowGFP with 50 µL of chemically competent or electrocompetent cells of Pro-auxotrophic E. coli K12-derived strain JM83 for transformation by the heat shock method or electroporation.

Mix 1 ng of each sample plasmid pQE-80L H6-KillerOrange with 50 µL of chemically competent or electrocompetent cells of Pro-auxotrophic E. coli K12-derived strain JM83 for transformation by the heat shock method or electroporation.
Recover the cells in 950 µL of SOC medium at 37 °C for 1 h.
Spread 50 µL of the recovered cells onto Luria Agar (LA) medium plates containing glucose and ampicillin.
Incubate the LA medium plates at 37 °C overnight or at 30 °C for 24 h.
Use a sterile pipette tip to select a single colony from an LA medium plate and resuspend the cells in 5 mL of Lysogeny Broth (LB) medium containing glucose and ampicillin.
Grow the cell culture overnight at 37 °C in an orbital shaker at 200-250 rpm.
Inoculate 200 mL of fresh NMM medium with all canonical l-amino acids and 100 µg/mL ampicillin using 2 mL of the overnight culture in a 2-L Erlenmeyer flask.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C in an orbital shaker at 220 rpm for ~3 h 30 min.
Measure the optical density at 600 nm (OD600) every 30 min until an OD600 value of ~0.7 is reached.
Determine OD600 in a spectrophotometer using a cuvette with a path length of 1 cm.
Use the corresponding cultivation medium for reference ("zero") measurement.
Inoculate fresh NMMΔPro medium supplemented with limited proline concentration.
Grow cells overnight at 37 °C in an orbital shaker at 220 rpm.
Perform OD600 determination every 30 min until differences are less than 0.05.
Spin down the cell suspension for 10 min at 3,000 x g and 4 °C.
Gently decant the supernatant into waste.
Resuspend cells in 50 mL of ice-cold NMMΔAA or NMMΔPro medium by careful pipetting.
Separate cells from medium by sedimentation at 4°C in a centrifuge at 3,000 x g for 10 minutes.
Gently decant the supernatant into waste.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 mL of NMMΔPro medium supplemented with 100 µg/mL ampicillin by gently pipetting up and down.
Incubate the suspension for 30 minutes at 37°C in an orbital shaker at 220 rpm to deplete proline completely.
Add an appropriate volume of either L-proline or R-Flp, S-Flp, Dfp, and Dhp from a 50 mM stock solution to adjust the final concentration to 1 mM in the cell suspension.
Add 0.5 mM IPTG from a 1 M stock solution to induce target protein expression.
Incubate overnight at 37°C in an orbital shaker at 220 rpm for protein expression.
Measure OD600 on the next day.
Thaw bacterial cell pellet on ice or at 4 °C in a 50 mL conical polystyrene tube for 10-20 min.
Add 10 mL of ice-cold binding buffer to the resuspended cells and gently pipette up and down to resuspend the cell pellet.
Add 100 µL of 50 mg/mL lysozyme to the cell suspension.
Add 100 µL of 1 mg/mL DNase I to the cell suspension.
Add 100 µL of 1 mg/mL RNase A to the cell suspension.
Add 30 µL of 1 M MgCl2 to the cell suspension.
Invert the cell suspension five times carefully.
Keep the closed tube on ice or at 4 °C for 60 min.
Sonicate the sample using an ultrasound homogenizer (e.g., three times for 3 min in a 50 mL polystyrene tube on an ice-water mixture, pulse 2 s/pause 4 s, 45% amplitude).
Centrifuge the sample for 60 min at 18,000 x g, 4 °C.
Pour the supernatant into a fresh 50 mL polystyrene tube.
Clear the supernatant using a membrane filter with 0.45 µm pore diameter.
Take a sample of "lysate" for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Add an equal volume of ddH2O as determined in substep 3.1.6 to resuspend the cell debris.
Take a sample of "pellet" for SDS-PAGE.
This corresponds to the "insoluble protein fraction".
Purify the sample using a 1 mL prepacked or self-packed IMAC FPLC column according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Set maximum column pressure to 0.3 MPa.
Set flow rate to 1 mL/min.
Use binding buffer for column equilibration.
Use wash buffer for the wash step.
Use elution buffer for target protein elution.
Alternatively, apply an automated FPLC system to elute the target protein with a linear imidazole concentration gradient (20-200 mM).
Collect and pool eluate fractions containing fluorescent proteins based on visible green or orange color.
Transfer pooled fractions into a dialysis membrane with a molecular weight cutoff of 5,000-10,000.
Dialyze at least three times against dialysis buffer or MS buffer.
Perform each round of dialysis for at least 2 hours.
Prepare a 1:100-fold dilution of the dialyzed elution fraction in PBS buffer.
Record the absorbance spectrum of diluted samples using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Calculate protein concentration based on the Lambert-Beer law formula.
Use literature values of molar extinction coefficients for specific wavelengths.
Prepare a reference measurement with dialysis buffer.
Take a sample of "eluate" for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Load 1-10 μg of protein per sample well for Coomassie Brilliant Blue-stained gels.
Determine absorbance A at 280 nm for samples "eluate", "lysate" and "pellet".
Adjust the probe volume to achieve A280nm = 2 by adding an appropriate amount of elution buffer (final probe volume should be at least 80 µL).
Mix the sample at a ratio of 4:1 (v/v) with 5x SDS loading dye buffer.
Boil the SDS samples at 95 °C for 5 min in a water bath or heat block to denature the proteins.
Allow the samples to cool down to RT and spin down the probes at 13,000 x g for 1 min prior to loading onto the gel.
Use 5-10 µL for Coomassie Brilliant Blue-stained SDS-PAGE.
Check the SDS-PAGE result carefully to ensure samples contain more than 95% of total protein in a band corresponding to the expected molecular weight.
Take a photograph of the Coomassie-stained gel.
Compare the intensity of the protein band of desired molecular weight with the intensity of all other bands in the lane by densitometry.
Use ImageJ software for densitometric evaluation of band intensities.
Carry out intact protein mass analysis by HPLC coupled to electrospray ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-ESI-TOF-MS).
Check the result from the SDS-PAGE experiment before fluorescence emission measurement to ensure sample purity is >95%.
Adjust the samples of each purified protein variant to a concentration of 0.3 µM using an appropriate absorbance value as reference.
Ensure that the approximate final sample volume is 200 μL.
Let the diluted samples equilibrate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Transfer the samples into a 1-cm quartz cuvette.
Measure a fluorescence emission spectrum of the samples using a fluorescence spectrometer.
Apply an excitation wavelength of 488 nm for EGFP.
Apply an excitation wavelength of 493 nm for NowGFP.
Apply an excitation wavelength of 510 nm for KillerOrange.
Check the result from the SDS-PAGE experiment to ensure sample purity is >95%.
Prepare two samples of 2 μL final volume at a concentration of 300 µM for each purified protein variant.
Add 18 μL of 1.11x PBS buffer containing 8.89 M urea and 5.56 mM DTT to the protein variant sample.
Incubate the samples for 5 minutes at 95 °C.
Dilute 20 µL samples 100-fold by adding 1980 µL of 1x PBS containing 5 mM DTT.
Transfer 200 µL of diluted sample into a 1-cm quartz cuvette.
Insert the quartz cuvette into an appropriate fluorescence spectrometer.
Monitor protein refolding in the samples by acquiring a fluorescence spectrum every 3 s over 30 min using 295 nm or 488 nm excitation wavelengths, depending on the variant.
Transfer the refolding samples into 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes after monitoring.
Store the samples at RT in the dark for 24 h to allow complete refolding of EGFP variants.
Measure fluorescence emission of refolded protein samples using the same excitation wavelength as before to capture the temporal endpoint of fluorescence recovery.
